question: When shipwrecked sailors killed one of their crew so three could live, what did an English court rule?
answer: Murder: necessity is no defence. In 1884 Dudley and Stephens killed Richard Parker, the 17-year-old cabin boy, to feed themselves and a third man. Lord Coleridge asked who is to judge such necessity, and by what measure lives are compared — here the weakest had been chosen. The death sentences were commuted to six months.
move: Never let the person who profits from an exception decide it applies.
reference: R v Dudley and Stephens (1884) 14 QBD 273; Simpson, Cannibalism and the Common Law, University of Chicago Press, 1984
